statement: J events are delivered only from blocks at least `depth` below the chain head, and a block that does not continue the delivered cursor is a reorg deeper than `depth`: a halt, never a rewrite.
source: consolidation-plan.md D9 and Q-X-10 (act on J events only at depth; a deeper reorg is a halt)

layers.arrival: n/a: the watcher is Host code that reads a node; the Arrival specs take J events as given
layers.quint: n/a: the watcher is Host code that reads a node; the Quint model takes J events as given
layers.contract: n/a: no contract code takes part; the watcher reads the deployed Depository's events
layers.rig: owed: test rig (a walk predicate for this rule; none is named yet)

killers.name: R-WATCH-DEPTH a head behind the cursor with no new blocks is an empty batch, not a fault
R-WATCH-DEPTH a head behind the cursor with a new block is too early
R-WATCH-DEPTH a block is delivered once the head is depth above it, and not before
R-WATCH-DEPTH a chain younger than its depth has nothing final: only a batch with no blocks is allowed
R-WATCH-DEPTH an empty batch is the cursor again: it announces the height it has and moves nothing
R-WATCH-DEPTH a depth below zero is refused when the watch starts
R-WATCH-DEPTH a first block whose parent is not the cursor's block is a reorg deeper than the depth
